messages:
leo: starting a canary for runtime build runtime-2026-03-kernel-optim1 against prod-like traffic now. noticed intermittent token-latency spikes on shard-7 within the first 10 minutes. cc @tara @sam

deploy-bot: canary deployed: runtime-2026-03-kernel-optim1 -> 3 instances on shard-7, traffic 5% (profile: canary-fast). start=1830004321

tara: saw the alert too. CPU on the canary hosts climbs to 92% then drops. not constant but correlates with long-tail sequence lengths.

sam: can you paste the pprof or stack traces? also which kernel variant is this — matmul-tiling v2?

leo: it's matmul-tiling-v2 + fused-attn-lw. quick log snippet: ```
[2026-03-10T15:05:12Z] shard-7-canary-1 tok_latency_p99=1450ms cpu=91% model_seq=2048
[2026-03-10T15:05:13Z] shard-7-canary-2 tok_latency_p99=1200ms cpu=87% model_seq=512
```

jin: hmm sequence length 2048 is rare for our canary profile. might be a sampling artifact from the load generator. can we narrow to real-prod traffic or reproduce with prometheus replay?

maya: starting a prometheus replay now against canary hosts with the same distribution as production-rt. will take ~4min.

tara: good. in parallel we should prepare a pin plan: if it keeps flapping we pin traffic back to runtime-2026-02-kernel-stable. want to avoid full rollback if only one kernel path is bad.

sam: agree. suggest: 1) scale canary to 0% quickly -> 0min impact 2) pin kernel variant on shard-7 to stable 3) run a controlled ramp for 30m 4) postmortem if regressions persist.

leo: can we do a targeted pin without touching other shards? Is deploy-bot able to pin kernel per-shard?

deploy-bot: command accepted: `pin kernel=runtime-2026-02-kernel-stable scope=shard-7`

leo: tested the pin in staging earlier; it should be safe. initiating p99/latency check after replay completes.

maya: replay done. canary hosts show reduced p99 after switching the runtime to pinned stable: ```
shard-7-canary-1 p99_before=1450ms p99_after=220ms
shard-7-canary-2 p99_before=1200ms p99_after=210ms
```

tara: that looks like the kernel change is the cause. decision: pin shard-7 to stable and abort further canary phases for this kernel variant. I'll file a rollback-notes entry and start a ticket to investigate fused-attn-lw path.

sam: please add to release notes: "kernel: matmul-tiling-v2 + fused-attn-lw caused p99 regressions for long sequences; pinned to runtime-2026-02-kernel-stable on affected shards; under investigation".

leo: I'll open an internal CI job to reproduce with targeted seq=2048 traces and run microbenchmarks. tagging @jin for kernel perf debug.

jin: on it. first suspicion is the micro-tiling path for non-power-of-two dims. will instrument and run locally. ETA 3 hours.

maya: ops note: we should add a canary flag to exclude extreme seq lengths from the default canary profile to avoid noisy signals. filing a quick PR.

tara: for transparency — scheduling a 20min post-mortem sync at 17:00 PT. invite: eng-runtime, eng-ml, oncall.

leo: ack. thanks everyone. marking thread resolved once pin check is green for 1h. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: pin applied successfully: kernel=runtime-2026-02-kernel-stable scope=shard-7 by leo at 1830004390.

sam: adding a rollback tag on the release branch and updating the changelog.

jin: initial repro shows a 3.6x perf delta on 2048 seq workloads for matmul-tiling-v2 on A100. deeper profiling next.

leo: saving logs and traces to the incident bucket: gs://redwood-ops/runtime-canary/1830004321/trace.tar.gz

tara: closing loop: if anyone sees a reappearance ping here. otherwise we keep kernel pinned until fix + QA. :eyes:
